pipeline_name: Badr El Din Spur Gas Pipelines

resolutions.researcher_notes: Egypt Oil & Gas report 'The Western Desert: Egypt's Giant Petroleum Reservoir' (egyptoil-gas.com, PDF, 2020) — url_verifier gives a raw-substring FAIL because it can't text-scan a compressed PDF binary (expected per verifier docstring); manually confirmed via pdftotext: the 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' table lists a row 'Badr El Din Spur (1) | Badr El Din Fields | BED/Abu Sennan connector | 130 | 20 | 180' (Length km / Diameter in / Capacity mmcf/d columns) — exact match to GEM's stated Length/Diameter/Capacity, confirming this is an in-service line in the report's current-infrastructure inventory (supports 'operating' by context; the word 'operating' itself is not literal in the table, consistent with confidence_tiers guidance that status is inferable). Companion landing page https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports/the-western-desert-egypts-giant-petroleum-reservoir/ verifies OK (200, contains 'Western Desert') and confirms report provenance/liveness. Only one independent source located confirming this exact segment as of the 2020 report date; no second, wholly independent corroboration found for THIS specific segment's status (tier: medium, single strong source).

Same PDF (pdftotext-confirmed): 'Badr El Din Spur (1)' is listed under the report's dedicated section 'NATURAL GAS INFRASTRUCTURE' / table 'Natural Gas Infrastructure in the Western Desert' (as distinct from the report's separate crude-oil pipeline table), confirming Fuel = Gas. url_verifier substring FAIL is the expected PDF-binary limitation, not a content miss (verified manually). Single-source (medium); fuel type is not in dispute (no conflicting source found calling this line an oil/products line).

Same PDF table row gives Capacity = 180 (mmcf/d column) for 'Badr El Din Spur (1)', matching GEM's Capacity=180.00 MMcf/d exactly. Confirmed via pdftotext extraction (raw-text row: 'Badr El Din Spur (1) / Badr El Din Fields / BED/Abu Sennan connector / 130 / 20 / 180'). No second independent source with a matching capacity figure was found for this specific segment (searched egyptoil-gas.com, OGJ, NS Energy, Petroleum Ministry — none name this spur by capacity); tier medium, single strong trade-press source with a clear tabulated figure.

Same PDF table row gives Length (Km column) = 130 for 'Badr El Din Spur (1)', matching GEM's LengthKnown=130.00 km exactly. Note: an unrelated OGJ CO2-EOR study (ogj.com/.../17240587) separately describes a distinct '130-mile, 16-in.' proposed CO2 pipeline to Abu Sennan — different unit (miles not km), different diameter (16in not 20in), and a different commodity/route (a 2013 CO2-injection proposal, not this in-service gas spur); flagging so it is not mistaken for corroboration of this row — it is not the same pipeline. Single-source (medium) for the 130km figure itself.

Same PDF table row gives Diameter (Inches column) = 20 for 'Badr El Din Spur (1)', matching GEM's Diameter=20.00 in exactly. See Length note re: an unrelated 16-in CO2 proposal pipeline in the same general area that is NOT this line. Single-source (medium).

Schema note: GEM's FuelSource cell value itself IS this URL (not a place/field name), so the corroborating fact needed here is simply that the URL is a real, resolvable, on-topic document — confirmed: HTTP HEAD returns 200 OK, Content-Type application/pdf, Content-Length 243193 bytes (matches downloaded copy); companion landing page https://egyptoil-gas.com/reports/the-western-desert-egypts-giant-petroleum-reservoir/ verifies OK via url_verifier (200 + 'Western Desert' present) and confirms this is the correct, currently-hosted Egypt Oil & Gas report (not a dead/retargeted link). pdftotext confirms the document is on-topic (covers Badr El Din/Abu Sennan gas infrastructure). Self-referential by construction (the ref IS the value), so 'independent' corroboration in the usual 2-source sense does not apply here.

Same PDF table row: From = 'Badr El Din Fields', To = 'BED/Abu Sennan connector', matching GEM's StartLocation='Badr El Din Field' / StartState-Province='Western Desert' / StartCountryOrArea='Egypt' and EndPrefecture/District='Abu Sennan' / EndCountryOrArea='Egypt'. The report situates both endpoints in the Western Desert's southern gas network (explicitly 'connecting Abu Sennan, Abu Gharadig, and Badr el Din Fields'). Could not independently corroborate the specific administrative attribution EndState/Province='Matruh' (Abu Sennan's governorate) from this source or any other found — flagging as a minor unverified sub-element within an otherwise well-supported location; not a contradiction, just unconfirmed by this reference. Single-source (medium).

Two independent sources place General Petroleum Co (GPC) as the operator/owner of the Abu Sennan gas plant/field that this spur feeds into: (1) the Western Desert PDF report states 'General Petroleum Company (GPC) established a plant for gas and condensate processing in Abu Sennan... the southern fields' production is linked to a distribution center on the Mediterranean Coast through Abu Sennan field' (pdftotext-confirmed, same table lists 'Badr El Din Spur (1)' running Badr El Din Fields -> BED/Abu Sennan connector, i.e. into this GPC-operated hub); (2) Oil & Gas Journal (url_verifier OK) independently states 'Abu Sennan field, which belongs to GPC' in a 2023-era CO2-EOR feasibility study. CAVEAT — neither source names the pipeline 'Badr El Din Spur (1)' or states GPC ownership of the LINE itself explicitly; the Owner=GPC/100% claim is corroborated at the field/hub level (both endpoints' operator context), not by a direct pipeline-ownership statement, so tier is capped at medium despite two independent agreeing sources. Also note: Badr El Din (BED) FIELD itself is operated by Shell/EGPC JV Badr El Din Petroleum Co (BAPETCO), NOT GPC — this is not a contradiction of the pipeline's Owner (a spur/gathering line's owner can differ from the upstream field's operator, and this line explicitly terminates at the GPC-operated Abu Sennan hub), but flagging so it isn't misread as GPC operating the BED field.
